boundary.rationale: 1.0 km (N-S) x 1.25 km (E-W). West edge just past Piața Victoriei (Antipa museum, Kiseleff start), north edge = Bd. Iancu de Hunedoara + one block (Str. Washington quiet), east edge = Calea Dorobanților / Str. Mihai Eminescu, south edge = Str. Biserica Amzei / Piața Amzei (quiet) so all of Piața Romană, Lascăr Catargiu, Piața Victoriei and Vasile Alecsandri are inside.

research.cross_section: Dual carriageway: 3 lanes each way (3.0–3.3 m), separated by a narrow raised central strip (≈1–2 m, kerbed, with lamp/trolley poles; left-turn pockets cut into it at signalised junctions → 4 lanes, e.g. "left|through|through|through"). Trolleybus overhead wires above the kerb-side lanes on both carriageways. No tram. No bus lane in OSM.

lanes.turn_pockets: left pocket NW-bound before Piața Victoriei (way 667696381); "through|through|through;right" before most side streets

research.parking: none on the carriageway (parking:both=no); cars park on side streets and in a small ADP lot (w874893780)
research.sidewalks: 4–6 m, grey concrete pavers with tree pits; kerb grey concrete
research.trees: continuous rows of mature linden (Tilia) and horse chestnut on both sidewalks (cities.js treeStreets) — crowns meet over the sidewalk; few on the median
research.lamps: grey steel poles ~10–12 m on both kerbs carrying LED heads and trolleybus span wires (verify on refs)
research.signals: signalised at Piața Victoriei, Grigore Alexandrescu, Clopotarii Vechi, Puțul de Piatră, Gheorghe Manu, Henri Coandă, Piața Romană; unsignalised right-in/right-out at Povernei, Viișoarei, Visarion, Constantin Daniel
landmarks_on_street: Statue of Lascăr Catargiu (Antonin Mercié, 1907; reinstalled 2011) at the Viișoarei/Povernei junction (≈44.4491, 26.0921)
Gheorghe Petrașcu House at the Piața Romană corner
Bucharest Astronomical Observatory "Amiral Vasile Urseanu" at no. 21 (dome on roof)
research.heritage: 12 listed houses along the boulevard (nos. 8, 12, 15, 21, 29, 39, 40, 50, 54, 56, 58 + Petrașcu House); the boulevard itself is listed as a historic monument
research.frontage_rule: alternating: 2–3-storey eclectic/neo-Romanian villas set back behind iron fences and gardens, and 6–9-storey interwar modernist apartment blocks (1929–1940, flat roofs, rounded corners, cream/grey render, steel windows) built to the sidewalk; few modern offices (Europe House). Many blocks carry seismic-risk class plaques (red dot "Bulină roșie" on class I).
research.transit: trolleybus 79, 86 (+ bus 100 airport express, 361, 381 on Lascăr Catargiu; 168, 226, 301, 331, 368 on Magheru)
research.history: part of the old Strada Colței; named Ana Ipătescu under communism

research.layout: Large oval one-way gyratory (counter-clockwise, 3–6 lanes with heavy turn-lane channelisation, e.g. "left|left|left;through|through|through|right") around a central green with lawns; 6 arteries meet: Calea Victoriei (S), Lascăr Catargiu (SE), Iancu de Hunedoara (E, tram), Aviatorilor/Kiseleff (N), Ion Mihalache (NW) and Nicolae Titulescu (W). Pasajul Victoria road underpass (1987–89) passes beneath W–E; metro Piața Victoriei (M1/M2 interchange) underneath with entrances A, B, C + lift.
research.signals: every arm signalised (OSM nodes 31402063, 31402056, 255721965, 1397123589, 257714748, 2404275892); signalised pedestrian crossings on each arm
research.trams: lines 1, 10 (and 46) run E–W across the square from Iancu de Hunedoara towards Titulescu/Ion Mihalache (central reservation)
research.frontage: NE: Palatul Victoria (Government) — long 3-storey stripped-classical travertine facade with arcaded ground floor and colonnade of slim piers, 2 recessed top floors; W: Grigore Antipa Natural History Museum (1903–06 neoclassical, columns, pediment) and Muzeul Țăranului Român behind; SW/S: 1992–94 apartment towers (Bl. D4/D5/D6/D7, 11–15 storeys) and Victoria Center (11 lv, 38.5 m) on Calea Victoriei; NW: BRD Tower and Bucharest Tower Center (one of the tallest buildings in Romania) on Bd. Ion Mihalache; parking lot opposite the Palace.
research.rooftop_signs: large rooftop/ façade advertising on the 1990s blocks facing the square and LED screens at the Calea Victoriei corner — brands rotate; take current ones from refs (pressone_ads documents >200 large ad installations in the centre incl. mesh banners covering whole facades)
research.congestion: one of the worst nodes in Bucharest at peaks (Victoriei–Unirii N–S axis named most congested)
research.conf: layout high (OSM, Wikipedia); rooftop brands unverified

research.cross_section: one-way eastbound, 1 lane (30 km/h zone in the hospital stretch) with parked cars; Grigore Alexandrescu children's hospital complex on the N side (Casa Ronald McDonald, burns clinic), villas and small offices on the S side

research.layout: Signalised square where Magheru (S, one-way N-bound arm 3–4 lanes + the S-bound arm), Lascăr Catargiu (NW) and Bd. Dacia (E–W) cross; traffic circulates around a small central island (former Capitoline Wolf statue site 1997–2010, statue moved to Bd. I.C. Brătianu). Metro M2 Piața Romană with entrances on Magheru.

Dacia.

top_local_details: Lascăr Catargiu is a DUAL carriageway, 3+3 lanes, with trolleybus wires — not a single 2-way road.
Vasile Alecsandri is a narrow ONE-WAY street southbound; UiPath's door is on its east side (The Landmark, no. 4) with Ted's Coffee + Friddi on the ground floor.
Europe House is a 2001–02 blue-green glass tower on the SW side near Piața Victoriei, with an Orange shop at the base.
Piața Victoriei is a huge oval gyratory with 6 arms, central lawns and an underpass (Pasajul Victoria) beneath.
Palatul Victoria = long pale travertine stripped-classical facade with arcade/colonnade, Romanian + EU flags.
The Antipa museum portico (columns + pediment) at the Kiseleff corner.
Trams (lines 1, 10) cross Piața Victoriei E–W along Iancu de Hunedoara in a central reservation.
Piața Romană: ASE dome to the NE, metro M2 entrances on Magheru, 5 to go kiosk, students everywhere.
Gheorghe Petrașcu House (neo-Romanian, Ion Mincu 1907) at the Romană / Lascăr corner.
Statue of Lascăr Catargiu (reinstalled 2011) midway along the boulevard at Povernei/Viișoarei.
Linden/chestnut canopies line Lascăr Catargiu; interwar modernist blocks alternate with fenced villas.
Red seismic-risk dots on some 1930s blocks (Lascăr Catargiu 7: urgency class I).
Speed limit 60 km/h on Lascăr Catargiu & Magheru; 50 elsewhere; 30 at the Grigore Alexandrescu hospital.
Calea Dorobanților south of Iancu de Hunedoara is one-way southbound with a contraflow bus lane.
Trolleybuses 79/86 on Lascăr Catargiu; airport express bus 100 too.
Cars parked on sidewalks of all side streets (Clopotarii Vechi, Grigore Alexandrescu, Vasile Alecsandri).
BRD Tower and Tower Center (very tall glass towers) dominate the NW skyline from Victoriei.
Sheraton tower (70 m, 1976) visible east of Piața Romană on Bd. Dacia.
Rooftop/facade ad banners and LED screens around both squares.
Embassies with guard booths (Iran at Lascăr Catargiu 39) and police station Secția 1 on the boulevard.
Big signalised junctions have countdown pedestrian signals and many zebra crossings.
Grey concrete paver sidewalks with metal bollards along boulevards; cracked asphalt on side streets.
Yellow STB trolleybuses (Solaris Trollino) and yellow taxis.
Astronomical observatory dome on the roof of Lascăr Catargiu 21.
Medicover clinic on Clopotarii Vechi; Grigore Alexandrescu children's hospital on the street of the same name.
Interwar blocks with rounded corners and horizontal balcony bands on Magheru.
Bd. Iancu de Hunedoara is lined with 9-storey 1960s–70s blocks.
Heavy peak congestion: Victoriei and Romană lock up 08–10 and 17–19.
The Landmark campus is a modern beige/grey block among old villas — contrast is striking.
Night: sodium-orange light on side streets vs white LED on boulevards (mixed).

driving.note: RO:urban default 50; several boulevards signed 60 (OSM maxspeed=60 on Lascăr Catargiu, Magheru, Dorobanți north).

markings.lane_line: white dashed 3 m line / 6 m gap on urban roads (RO standard SR 1848-7), 0.10–0.15 m wide
markings.centre_line: white continuous (single) on 2-lane two-way, double continuous on 4+ lane two-way without median
markings.zebra: white bars 0.5 m wide / 0.5 m gap, parallel to traffic, no side lines; a few school-zone crossings have red infill between the white bars (verify per crossing on refs)
markings.bus_lane: white continuous line with "BUS" text; since 2019 some STB lanes on Magheru axis/Ștefan cel Mare painted red-brown (#9E3B2E) – verify per street
markings.yellow: yellow only for temporary works and kerb no-parking (zig-zag at bus stops)
markings.wear: markings visibly worn/faded on most streets except freshly resurfaced arteries — use 60–80% opacity

kerbs.material: grey concrete kerbstones 15×25 cm (older streets: granite #8C8C8C), kerb height 12–18 cm, often chipped

sidewalks.paving: mix: (a) grey concrete interlocking pavers ("pavele") #A9A59C on renovated boulevards; (b) cracked asphalt #6E6C68 on side streets; (c) 40×40 grey concrete slabs on 1960–80s estates
sidewalks.parking_on_sidewalk: very common: cars half/fully on the sidewalk on side streets, behind metal bollards on boulevards

traffic_lights.model: RO 3-aspect vehicle heads (200/300 mm), black or yellow housing with yellow-black backplates on main arteries, mounted on grey/black poles + overhead mast arms at big junctions; pedestrian 2-aspect (red/green man) with countdown displays on major junctions

street_name_plates.style: blue plate (#1F4E9A) white text "Bulevardul X" + sector number "Sector 1" in smaller text, on building corners or poles

bus_shelter.style: STB/Clear-channel style glass shelters with grey steel frame and backlit ad panel; many stops have only a pole with the yellow STB stop sign + timetable

metro_totem.style: Metrorex entrance: blue square sign with white "M", station name in white on blue; stairs down with grey stone/steel railings

trolleybus_wires.style: pair of copper contact wires 0.6 m apart per direction at ~5.6 m, carried by span wires between steel or concrete poles on both kerbs (often shared with street lamps)

tram_track.style: standard gauge 1435 mm; on boulevards in a central reservation with concrete sleepers/ballast or grass, kerbed and fenced in places; overhead single contact wire on span wires
